::: {#def-single-world .theorem}
## Single-world independence

For a value $\mathbf{pa}$ of the parents of $V$, the one-step-ahead counterfactual of $V$ is

$$
V^{(\mathbf{pa})}=f_V\big(\mathbf{pa},U_V\big),
$$

the value $V$ takes when its parents are set to $\mathbf{pa}$. For every $\mathbf{v}$ in the range of $\mathbf{V}$, write $\mathbf{pa}_V(\mathbf{v})$ for the values in $\mathbf{v}$ of the parents of $V$. Single-world independence holds if, for every $\mathbf{v}$, the one-step-ahead counterfactuals

$$
\big\{V^{(\mathbf{pa}_V(\mathbf{v}))}:V\in\mathbf{V}\big\}
$$

are mutually independent. Equivalently, let $\Gamma_{\mathbf{v}}$ be the static regime that sets every variable to its value in $\mathbf{v}$: the natural values of the variables of $\big(\mathcal{M},\mathcal{M}^{(\Gamma_{\mathbf{v}})}\big)$, obtained by sequential substitution, are mutually independent, since the natural value of $V$ under $\Gamma_{\mathbf{v}}$ is $V^{(\mathbf{pa}_V(\mathbf{v}))}$.
:::
